source_refs.note: Instantaneous Displacement: a main subheading of 14.4 Simple Harmonic Motion and Uniform Circular Motion, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 26-26.

blocks.text: If A is the initial position of particle P, then the angle which the radius OP sweeps out in time t is θ = ωt with OQ as shown in Fig. 14.5.

blocks.alt: A circle of radius xo with centre O and horizontal diameter ending at A. A point P on the circle moves anticlockwise with angular velocity omega; the radius OP makes the angle theta = omega t with OA. Q is the foot of the perpendicular from P on the diameter, and x = OQ is the displacement of Q from O.
blocks.caption: Figure 14.5: A point P moving on circular path at constant angular velocity (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 14.5).

blocks.text: Equation (14.11) gives the instantaneous displacement of point Q which is executing simple harmonic motion.
